A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Go-with-the-Flow and contain complete, readable main texts and supplementary material. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original noise-warping benchmarks, video-generation experiments, ablations, and a 40-participant user study in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: V4 retains those original empirical results and adds quantitative local-motion comparisons, additional baselines, and new ablation results in Table 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, noise degradation, latent-space downsampling, fine-tuning objectives, and inference procedures are unchanged. The CogVideoX-2B experiment tests the existing procedure with another model size; the appendix pseudocode is identical.

E1.justification: V4 adds the dataset labeled VIPSeg for the existing local object motion-control task. Quantitative evaluation of the existing 40 user-study videos does not establish another new population or task. The other training and evaluation datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds MotionCtrl to DAVIS T2V comparisons and ImageConductor to I2V comparisons on DAVIS, DL3DV, and WonderJourney. These introduce training-based competitors into comparisons previously using DMT and/or MotionClone. The local-control comparators SG-I2V, MotionClone, and DragAnything were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: V4 introduces optical-flow error as an evaluation metric and quantitative protocols for local object control. New evaluation configurations vary degradation strength, training-data fractions of 33% and 12.5%, and the base model from 5B to 2B. The retained main training budget is unchanged; the new optical-flow-error metric's computation is not specified.

E4.justification: Section 4.4.3 replaces the DL3DV low-LoRA-rank and no-degradation ablations with a quantitative DAVIS degradation sweep, training-data-size ablations, and a CogVideoX-2B comparison. The control without motion conditioning remains under the label Original CogVideoX-5B. Existing qualitative degradation examples and appendix analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The Moran's I and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, reported p-values, 40-participant study, and appendix preference charts are unchanged. V4 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds local-control, optical-flow-error, comparator, and ablation results while removing two DL3DV ablation rows. For example, VIPSeg FID is 41.1 for Ours versus 61.4 for SG-I2V; newly added MotionCtrl exceeds Ours in DAVIS T2V subject consistency, 0.97 versus 0.88. Shared results are retained with equivalent rounding or unit changes, and Table 1 is unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gaussianity and time-complexity propositions, Algorithm 1 mathematics, noise-degradation formula, appendix proof, and expansion-contraction recovery example are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: architecture-agnostic motion conditioning, efficient Gaussianity-preserving noise warping, and advantages across motion-control applications. The additional experiments support existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: V4 removes explanations of low-rank adaptation failure and artifacts caused by inaccurate flow under strong conditioning. It adds data/model-size interpretations and recommends gamma around 0.5. However, Section 4.4.3 now incorrectly states that increasing gamma tightens control, contradicting Section 3.3 and Table 2: mIoU falls from 0.74 at gamma 0.5 to 0.50 at 0.9.

D1.justification: V4 updates project/code destinations, explicitly identifies AnimateDiff weights and a community HunyuanVideo version in Appendix 11, and labels the retained DAVIS I2V setting as gamma 0.5. Main hardware, training hyperparameters, preprocessing, and pseudocode remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds references for ImageConductor and VSPW, the latter cited as the source for VIPSeg. MotionCtrl was already cited in v1 but becomes an evaluated competitor. The related-work narrative and core novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the experimental comparison and ablation paragraphs, with a brief appendix addition and changes to labels and references. The section order, introductory narrative, method exposition, and conclusion are preserved.

P2.justification: Table 2 is substantially restructured with local-control blocks, training-free and optical-flow columns, shaded final-model rows, dashed ablation separators, and a rescaled FVD heading. Figure 4 expands from one column to full width, and Figure 5 moves alongside Figure 6. The qualitative image panels and appendix figures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 adds quantitative evidence where local control previously relied on qualitative examples and user preferences, and strengthens motion-transfer comparisons with MotionCtrl and ImageConductor. Data-size and model-size ablations also improve empirical assessment. These gains modestly outweigh the removal of useful LoRA/no-degradation analyses and flow-mismatch limitations, together with the new, incorrect interpretation of gamma in Section 4.4.3.
